outcome: Anorectal manometry (ARM) findings (maximum resting pressure, squeeze pressure increment (SPI))
Three-dimensional endoanal ultrasonography (3D-EAUS) findings (circumferential extension of defect for EAS and IAS, EAS, IAS and total Starck scores)
cohort: The study included all consecutive women who sustained an obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASIS) between 2015 and 2020 and underwent primary repair.
finding: Both anorectal manometry (ARM) and endoanal ultrasonography (EAUS) findings after OASIS are directly related to each other and associated with postpartum symptoms.
